BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r1.claim: The condemned cry for help loudly; the intensive form of the verb derives from shouting, with the inserted emphatic letter strengthening its force, and is used for seeking intercession.

BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r2.claim: They ask to return to worldly life and do righteous deeds, meaning to believe instead of disbelieving and obey instead of sinning, since deeds are accepted only with faith.

BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r3.claim: Their qualification that they will do deeds unlike their former ones reveals that they had mistaken whim, instinct, and opposition for righteousness.

BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r4.claim: The question rebukes them: God gave them enough time and a span in which anyone willing could remember; the wording may mean a period or a time in general.

BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r5.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r5.claim: Kashifi takes the phrase as asking whether they were given a lifespan long enough for reflection by anyone willing to remember.

BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r6.claim: Reflection means having the opportunity to consider one’s condition and amend it; after puberty, reason opens, requiring people to infer the Creator from creation, and the duty intensifies around eighteen or twenty.

BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r7.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r7.claim: A report says God leaves no excuse to a person whose life He extends until sixty years.

BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r8.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r8.claim: The Prophet said the community’s lifespans range from sixty to seventy, with few exceeding that; after sixty, old age makes seventy the final period for reflection.

BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r9.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v7p277#2/r9.claim: A daily and nightly caller warns people at forty that the harvest is near, at sixty to account for what they sent ahead, and at seventy to come to reckoning.

BURSEVI:v7p278/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p278/r1.speaker: عبد القادر الكيلاني
BURSEVI:v7p278/r1.claim: To a young penitent, Abd al-Qadir says God summoned him, preserved him despite his turning away, and moved him toward divine nearness and intimacy.

BURSEVI:v7p278/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p278/r2.speaker: عبد القادر الكيلاني
BURSEVI:v7p278/r2.claim: To an elderly penitent, he says youth and adulthood were met with pardon and delay, but estrangement in old age brought displeasure; return will still be accepted.

BURSEVI:v7p278/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p278/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p278/r3.claim: A Persian couplet contrasts the youthful who hurry toward spiritual gain with old age, whose coldness prevents the vessel from advancing.

BURSEVI:v7p278/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p278/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p278/r4.claim: Companions and their successors intensified worship and night prayer at forty or on seeing gray hair, reduced social contact, and left their beds; no age is safe because death’s time is hidden.

BURSEVI:v7p278/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p278/r5.speaker: الجمهور
BURSEVI:v7p278/r5.claim: The majority identify the warner as the Messenger; alternatives are the Qur’an, reason distinguishing good from evil, deaths among family and neighbors, or gray hair.

BURSEVI:v7p278/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p278/r6.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v7p278/r6.claim: Kashifi says many scholars identify gray hair as the warner, since it signals life’s flame waning and the mirror of one’s being turning white.

BURSEVI:v7p278/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p278/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p278/r7.claim: A report says Abraham was the first of Adam’s descendants to gray; God called gray hair dignity in this world and light in the next, and Abraham asked for more.

BURSEVI:v7p278/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p278/r8.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v7p278/r8.claim: A hadith says God dislikes an old man whose hair has not turned gray, as explained in al-Maqasid al-Hasana.

BURSEVI:v7p279/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p279/r1.speaker: الكواشي
BURSEVI:v7p279/r1.claim: Al-Kawashi allows every sign warning of departure from life to count as a warner and calls for heedfulness when it appears.

BURSEVI:v7p279/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p279/r2.speaker: محمد بن الحسن
BURSEVI:v7p279/r2.claim: The sounder view attributed to Muhammad al-Shaybani makes Hajj an expanded duty that may be delayed unless delay is likely to cause it to be missed; sudden death brings no sin, but clear warning makes delay impermissible.

BURSEVI:v7p279/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p279/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p279/r3.claim: The condemned beg to return for the whole span of worldly existence; God answers that He gave them life and sent a warner, yet they admit they had both.

BURSEVI:v7p279/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p279/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p279/r4.claim: The command to taste punishment follows from God’s granting life and sending a warner; the wrongdoers are those who wronged themselves through disbelief and idolatry, with no defender to repel punishment.

BURSEVI:v7p279/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p279/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p279/r5.claim: Ishari reading: people were asleep in worldly heedlessness and only awaken fully after death and resurrection, when they taste and perceive punishment.

QUSHAYRI:v3p71/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p71/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p71/r1.claim: The damned ask to leave Hell and act righteously, but are answered that they had a life long enough for reflection and a warner.

QUSHAYRI:v3p71/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p71/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p71/r2.claim: Another gloss asks whether they had completed the respite in which they could consider evidence.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p138/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p138/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p138/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says a lifespan long enough for reflection is sixty years.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p138/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p138/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p138/r2.claim: The Prophet says God has given a person sufficient warning by granting life for sixty or seventy years.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r6.claim: The verb «يصطرخون» is an intensive form from ṣarakh, with tāʾ changed to ṭāʾ; ṣarākh is a loud cry, also used for appealing for help.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r7.claim: Their plea asks to leave Hell and return to worldly life.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r8.claim: He explains the promised righteous deed as professing «لا إله إلا الله», abandoning shirk, believing instead of disbelieving, and obeying instead of sinning.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r9.claim: He asks why the request adds «other than what we used to do» after «righteous deeds», and whether it implies a different righteous deed; Abū Ḥayyān says it conveys regret and admission.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r10.claim: The added phrase intensifies regret for their former wrong; its apparent implication disappears because they had treated shirk and sins as good and now seek different conduct.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r11.claim: A report says they receive this answer after a period equal to worldly life; «أولم نعمركم» is a rebuke, confirmation, and reminder.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r12.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36/r12.claim: Most read «ما يتذكر»; al-Aʿmash reads «ما يذكر» by assimilation from «اذكر», pronouncing the initial hamzat al-waṣl in connected recitation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r1.claim: He identifies the lifetime sufficient for reflection as the age of maturity, the beginning of discernment.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r2.claim: He gives eighteen years as the lifetime sufficient for reflection.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r3.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r3.claim: He gives twenty years as the lifetime sufficient for reflection.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r4.claim: He gives forty years; other reported ages are seventeen, fifty, and sixty, the last attributed to ʿAlī and also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r5.claim: «And a warner came to you» coordinates with «Did We not give you life?», whose implied meaning is affirmative, as in the cited Qurʾānic examples.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r6.claim: «The warner» is generic for the prophets, each warning his own community; another recitation has the plural «النذر».

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس، وعكرمة، وسفيان، ووكيع، والحسن بن الفضل، والفراء، والطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p36#2/r7.claim: They explain the warner as gray hair; other explanations are deaths among relatives and reaching extreme old age.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#9/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#9/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#9/r2.claim: Some say the warner is gray hair, meaning people were given life until they turned gray.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r1.claim: Yaṣṭarikhūn is an iftiʿāl form of ṣarākh, intense shouting, with original tāʾ changed to ṭāʾ; it often means calling for rescue.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r2.claim: Qatāda says they seek rescue from God; the suggestion they call to one another in bewilderment is rejected.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r3.claim: Their plea may be introduced by implied ‘saying’ and coordinated with prior speech, stand independently as an explanation, or function as a circumstantial phrase.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r4.claim: Calling requested work different from former work expresses regret and desire to repair admitted wrongdoing; alternatively, they mistakenly thought past conduct good.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r5.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ offers parses making ṣāliḥan and ghayra modifiers of omitted nouns, or ṣāliḥan a modifier and ghayra the object of ‘we do.’

ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r6.claim: They ask to leave Hell and return to worldly life for righteous work, especially affirming God’s unity, obeying the Messenger, and submitting.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains ‘we do righteous work’ as saying lā ilāha illā Allāh.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r8.claim: The divine question rebukes their plea and denies God failed to give ample time for reflection and reminders.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r9.claim: Mā means the age or span of years in which anyone wishing to remember could reflect and be reminded.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r10.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v22p200#2/r10.claim: Abū Ḥayyān takes mā as a temporal verbal noun; this is challenged because fīhi cannot refer to it unless treated as a noun or refers to age implied by ‘We gave you long life.’

ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r1.speaker: ابن الحاجب
ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r1.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib says making mā negative is untenable in wording and meaning.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r2.speaker: علي وابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r2.claim: A report from ʿAlī, authenticated by al-Ḥākim from Ibn ʿAbbās, sets sufficient lifetime at sixty; Sahl ibn Saʿd reports God keeps a person alive to sixty to remove excuses.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r3.claim: Other estimates are fifty, forty-six (Ibn ʿAbbās), forty or puberty (al-Ḥasan), seventeen, eighteen (Qatāda), twenty (ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz), and twenty to sixty (Mujāhid).

ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r4.speaker: الأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r4.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads mā yadhkur fīhi man udhkira with assimilation and pronounces the connecting hamzat al-waṣl in connected speech.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r5.claim: ‘The warner came to you’ coordinates with the question’s meaning, effectively ‘We gave you life and the warner came’; another parse coordinates it with ‘We gave you life.’

ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r6.speaker: السدي وابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r6.claim: Al-Suddī and Ibn Zayd identify the warner as Muḥammad; another view says the Qur’an, while Abū Ḥayyān takes all prophets, supported by the plural al-nudhur.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وسفيان بن عيينة ووكيع والحسين بن الفضل والفراء والطبري
ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r7.claim: These authorities say the warner is gray hair; a report makes each white hair warn its neighbor of death, and poetry likewise calls gray hair a herald.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r8.claim: Other warners are fever, deaths of relatives, or maturity of reason; the singular ‘warner’ fits the immediate point.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p201/r9.claim: The command to taste punishment follows from long life and the warner’s arrival; denial of a helper is causal, ‘wrongdoers’ means unbelievers, and naming them rebukes them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p424#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p424#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p424#2/r4.claim: يصطرخون means crying for help; the form comes from ṣarākh, a cry, and they ask to leave the Fire and replace their past deeds with good ones.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425/r1.claim: The reflection-time is identified as puberty; ʿAṭāʾ, Qatāda, and al-Kalbī say eighteen years, al-Ḥasan forty, and Ibn ʿAbbās sixty, transmitting from ʿAlī.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425/r2.claim: The Prophet says God has excused a person whose life He extended to sixty years.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425/r3.claim: A report from the Prophet says the community’s lifespans range from sixty to seventy, with few exceeding that.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425#2/r1.claim: Most exegetes identify the warner as Muhammad; another view says the Qur’an.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425#2/r2.speaker: عكرمة وسفيان بن عيينة ووكيع
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425#2/r2.claim: The warner is gray hair: people were given time until gray, a sign warning of death.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425#2/r3.claim: A transmitted saying has each white hair tell another to prepare because death is near.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p425#2/r4.claim: The wrongdoers are told to taste punishment because they have no helper.

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:37/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:37/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:37/r1.claim: They cry out loudly for help; the verb comes from the root meaning a shout, used for pleading because sufferers raise their voices.

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:37/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:37/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:37/r2.claim: Their plea to do different righteous deeds admits that their earlier conduct was not righteous, though they had thought it so, and that they now regret it.

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:37/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:37/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:37/r3.claim: God rebukes them: their life had allowed reflection, and the reminder could be the Prophet, scripture, reason, gray hair, or deaths of relatives.

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:37/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:37/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:37/r4.claim: The Prophet reports that sixty years is the age by which God has fully excused a person.

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:37/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:37/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:37/r5.claim: No helper can ward off the punishment from wrongdoers.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r1.claim: The damned scream with all their strength and ask God to bring them out so they can do righteous deeds instead of their former work, either admitting error or regretfully recognizing they were wrong.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r2.claim: God reminds them that he gave them sufficient life and reason, delayed their punishment, and allowed any capable person time to mend their affairs; the past tense implies the register of those who remember is closed after resurrection.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas is cited for sixty years as the period sufficient for reflection; al-Bukhari placed the report in the opening chapters of al-Riqaq.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that one whom God allows to reach sixty has received sufficient warning regarding lifespan; the author cites Ahmad ibn Maniʿ.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that the lifespans of his community range from sixty to seventy years, with few exceeding that; the author cites al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, and Abu Yaʿla.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r6.claim: Messengers and revealed books supplied warnings that reinforce what reason alone could not establish; after that evidence, the wrongdoers are told to taste their eternal torment, with no helper to rescue them.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p229/r7.claim: The no-helper statement applies to every wrongdoer: whenever injustice becomes established, it weakens while truth gains strength.

DURR-FULL:v7p30/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p30/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p30/r3.claim: Qatada says the people in Hell cry out for help.

DURR-FULL:v7p30/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p30/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p30/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the period of life in which a person could reflect as sixty years; a Prophetic report asks where the sixty-year-olds are on Judgment Day.

DURR-FULL:v7p30/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p30/r5.speaker: سهل بن سعد
DURR-FULL:v7p30/r5.claim: The Prophet says God has excused no one whose life was extended until sixty; a second report says reaching sixty means God has fully given a person an excuse.

DURR-FULL:v7p31/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p31/r1.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v7p31/r1.claim: Ali says the life granted to them as a proof was sixty years; Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet said sixty years is a full excuse and most of the community live sixty to seventy.

DURR-FULL:v7p31/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p31/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p31/r2.claim: Mujahid says the relevant lifetime is sixty years; Ibn Abbas gives forty-six and al-Hasan gives forty years.

DURR-FULL:v7p31/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p31/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p31/r3.claim: Qatada says long life itself is evidence and asks God for refuge from being reproached for it; he notes an eighteen-year-old was among them and says lifespan and messengers were arguments against them.

DURR-FULL:v7p31/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p31/r4.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v7p31/r4.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the warner as Muhammad; Ibn Zayd agrees and cites another verse calling him a warner from earlier warners.

DURR-FULL:v7p31/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p31/r5.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v7p31/r5.claim: ʿIkrima and Ibn Abbas identify the warner as gray hair.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r1.claim: Qatadah glosses their cries in Hell as calling for help.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r2.claim: The Prophet says that on Resurrection people will ask where the sixty-year-olds are; sixty is the age meant for reflection.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r3.claim: The Prophet says God has given a person an excuse by extending his life until sixty.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says the period in which a person might reflect is forty years.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r5.claim: Qatadah calls long life a proof against people and seeks refuge from its being used to reproach them.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r6.claim: Qatadah says the verse was revealed when an eighteen-year-old was among them.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r7.claim: Qatadah says the warning against them was both their lifespan and the messengers.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r8.claim: The Prophet says that whoever reaches sixty has been given sufficient lifetime warning by God.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r9.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r9.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the warner as Muhammad.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3184#2/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd also identifies the warner as Muhammad and cites the earlier warning in 53:56.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3185/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3185/r1.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3185/r1.claim: Ikrimah identifies the warner as gray hair.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p318/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p318/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p318/r6.claim: The pronoun refers to those who disbelieved in 35:36, and the clause is coordinated with ‘they have the Fire of Hell’; it is not circumstantial because the preceding conclusion closes that discourse.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p318/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p318/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p318/r7.claim: Yaṣṭarikhūn intensifies yaṣrukhūn: they scream with great effort because of what has befallen them; their plea explains the screaming and displays their helplessness.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p318/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p318/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p318/r8.claim: Their promise to do good if released is belated repentance; the jussive yaʿmal ṣāliḥan answers the plea with the understood condition ‘if You release us.’

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p318/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p318/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p318/r9.claim: Calling their future deeds different from what they did before expresses regret: they now know their former deeds were false and harmful in the realm of realities.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p319/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p319/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p319/r1.claim: Taʿmīr is prolonging a life; the related expression ‘a time’ is a temporal, masdar-based adverbial phrase.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p319/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p319/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p319/r2.claim: The clause ‘whoever reflects in it’ describes a span of time sufficient for reflection and instruction.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p319/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p319/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p319/r3.claim: The warner is Muhammad; calling him a warner highlights the aspect of his mission most relevant to these people.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p319/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p319/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p319/r4.claim: ‘Your warner came’ coordinates with the preceding question because it conveys an assertion; coordinating an assertion with an interrogative form is valid here.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p319/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p319/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p319/r5.claim: The fāʾ in ‘taste’ marks consequence, its object ‘the punishment’ is omitted, and the imperative conveys their continuing punishment and inability to escape.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p320/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p320/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p320/r1.claim: ‘The wrongdoers have no helper’ may continue the rebuke, ending their hope of rescue and asking where their supposed allies are.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p320/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p320/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p320/r2.claim: Alternatively it is a separate conclusion for listeners, making the rule apply to every wrongdoer, including the disbelievers just described.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p320/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p320/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p320/r3.claim: Wrongdoing violates a rights-holder's due; its gravest form is shirk, an assault on God's oneness and on the self by leading it into punishment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p320/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p320/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p320/r4.claim: The generality of wrongdoers and helpers means helping an oppressor violates justice; the community must restrain wrongdoing, refuting the pre-Islamic maxim to help one's brother whether wrongdoer or victim.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p320/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p320/r5.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p320/r5.claim: The Prophet corrected that maxim: helping an unjust person means restraining him from his injustice.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r7.claim: Yaṣṭarikhūn derives from ṣurākh; its original form was yaṣtarikhūn, with tāʾ changed to ṭāʾ because the articulations are close. Their request to return is followed by a rebuke.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r8.claim: The omitted words mean that they say, Our Lord; the response, Did We not give you a lifetime, is a question of censure. Mā is temporal.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r9.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the age that permits reflection begins at puberty, the first stage of mature recollection.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r10.claim: Qatada sets the threshold for remembering at eighteen years.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r11.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r11.claim: Another group sets the threshold at twenty years.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r12.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r12.claim: Al-Zajjāj transmits seventeen years as the threshold.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p440#2/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās sets the threshold at forty; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this a good view and cites reports about reaching forty without repentance.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r1.speaker: الشاعر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r1.claim: A poem warns that a person who reaches forty without modesty or restraint should be left to the course he chose.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r2.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r2.claim: Some set the age threshold at fifty; two cited poems portray fifty as advanced age and a short distance from death.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others say sixty is the threshold and an excuse; Ibn ʿAṭiyya regards this as a sound, apt view.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r4.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r4.claim: A report says that on Resurrection Day a call will ask where the sixty-year-olds are.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r5.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r5.claim: A Prophetic report says that God has left a person no excuse once granting sixty years of life.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r6.speaker: الأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r6.claim: The majority reads mā yatadhakkaru fīhi man tadhakkar; al-Aʿmash instead reads mā yudhakkaru fīhi man adhkar.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r7.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r7.claim: Most commentators identify the warner as the prophets, each warning their own people and contemporaries; Muhammad warns the later world.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r8.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p441/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports the alternative that the warner is gray hair; Ibn ʿAṭiyya considers this a good view but says binding proof comes through scriptural warning.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r1.claim: يصطرخون is an intensive form derived from crying out; they beg to be released so they can affirm God's oneness and obey instead of committing idolatry and sins.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r2.claim: The question Have We not given you a long life is rhetorical confirmation, not a request for information.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r3.claim: One view says the life span was seventy years; the verse rebukes those who reached seventy.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r4.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r4.claim: Another view gives forty years; Hasan and Ibn al-Sa'ib also hold this duration.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r5.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r5.claim: A further view gives sixty years.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r6.speaker: عطاء ووهب بن منبه وأبو العالية وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r7.speaker: ابن عمر وعكرمة وسفيان بن عيينة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r7.claim: One interpretation of the warner is gray hair, a sign that they had lived long enough.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r8.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد وابن السائب ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r8.claim: A second interpretation of the warner is the Prophet.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r9.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p494/r9.claim: Two further interpretations of the warner are the death of family members and fever.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p495/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p495/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p495/r1.claim: ذوقوا means taste the punishment; the wrongdoers have no protector who can prevent it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p552#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p552#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p552#3/r1.claim: Hell's people cry out for return to do good, but God knows they would repeat their former sins; He refuses their plea, as also stated in 40:11–12.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p552#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p552#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p552#3/r2.claim: Their allotted lives were long enough for anyone willing to benefit from truth to remember it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p553/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p553/r1.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p553/r1.claim: Ibn Jarīr selects the report from Ibn ʿAbbās that the age at which a person is given enough time to reflect is forty years.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p553/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p553/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p553/r2.claim: A second route from Ibn ʿAbbās gives sixty years; Ibn Kathīr says this report is sounder and correct, supported by hadith.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p553/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p553/r3.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p553/r3.claim: ʿAlī also identifies sixty years as the age meant by the verse.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p553/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p553/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p553/r4.claim: A Prophetic report from Ibn ʿAbbās says those reaching sixty will be called on Judgment Day, referring to the age in this verse.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p553/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p553/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p553/r5.claim: Ibn Kathīr questions the report about the call to sixty-year-olds because of Ibrāhīm ibn al-Faḍl's condition.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p553/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p553/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p553/r6.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra says God has excused a person who reaches sixty or seventy years.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p554/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p554/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p554/r1.claim: A route through Abū Ḥāzim and Abū Hurayra reports that a person reaching sixty has received God's full excuse in life.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p554/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p554/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p554/r2.claim: Al-Bazzār transmits from Abū Hurayra the report that sixty years is the age at which God has excused a person.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p554/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p554/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p554/r3.claim: A route through Ibn ʿAjlān from Abū Hurayra says that anyone reaching sixty has been given an excuse in life.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p554/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p554/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p554/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr accepts the hadith through these routes, preferring al-Bukhārī's authentication over al-Ṭabarī's reservation.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p555/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p555/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p555/r1.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra says life's struggle falls between sixty and seventy and few of the community reach seventy; Ibn Kathīr calls its chain weak.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p555/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p555/r2.speaker: الأطباء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p555/r2.claim: Some physicians say natural lifespan is 120 years, with growth until sixty and decline and senility thereafter; an unnamed poet's verse illustrates the loss of youthful pleasure by sixty.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p555/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p555/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p555/r3.claim: A report says the community's lifespans are generally sixty to seventy, with few exceeding that; al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah transmit it, and al-Tirmidhī calls it ḥasan gharīb.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556/r1.speaker: البزار
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556/r1.claim: Al-Bazzār says the report about the community's age span is unique through this chain and its transmitter ʿUthmān ibn Maṭar is weak.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556/r2.speaker: حذيفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556/r2.claim: Ḥudhayfa asks the Prophet about the community's lifespans; the reply gives fifty to sixty and invokes God's mercy on those reaching seventy or eighty.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556/r3.claim: The Prophet's lifespan is most famously reported as sixty-three years, though sixty and sixty-five are also reported.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وأبو جعفر الباقر وقتادة وسفيان بن عيينة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, al-Bāqir, Qatāda, and Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna identify the warner as gray hair.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556/r5.speaker: السدي وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556/r5.claim: Al-Suddī and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd identify the warner as the Messenger; Ibn Zayd cites 53:56.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556/r6.speaker: قتادة وابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556/r6.claim: A sounder report from Qatāda says both a long lifetime and the messengers were used as proof; Ibn Jarīr prefers the Messenger interpretation, supported by 43:77–78, 17:15, and 67:8–9.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p556#2/r1.claim: They are told to taste the punishment for disobeying the prophets during their lives; no helper can rescue them from torment, restraints, and chains.

JISHUMI:v8p5854/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5854/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5854/r4.claim: Istirakh is a cry for help; the derived form shifts tāʾ to ṭāʾ after ṣād to balance the sounds in articulation and emphasis.

JISHUMI:v8p5855/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r3.claim: In Hell, they cry loudly for help and ask to return so they can do righteous deeds instead of their former deeds.

JISHUMI:v8p5855/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، مسروق
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r4.claim: One report says the lifetime that allows reflection is forty years.

JISHUMI:v8p5855/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r5.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas sets that lifetime at sixty years and is transmitted as a Prophetic report.

JISHUMI:v8p5855/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits from the Prophet that most of his community live between sixty and seventy; another Prophetic report says deaths occur most often in that range.

JISHUMI:v8p5855/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r7.speaker: ابن زيد، أبو علي
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd, Abu Ali, and others identify the warner as the Prophet; the author prefers this literal reading.

JISHUMI:v8p5855/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r8.speaker: زيد بن علي
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r8.claim: Zayd b. Ali interprets the warner as the Qur'an.

JISHUMI:v8p5855/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r9.speaker: عكرمة، سفيان بن عيينة، وكيع
JISHUMI:v8p5855/r9.claim: Ikrima, Sufyan b. Uyayna, and Wakiʿ interpret the warner as gray hair.

JISHUMI:v8p5857/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5857/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5857/r1.claim: People can make amends during worldly life, but they cannot do so in the afterlife; the question about their lifetime is a reproach.

JISHUMI:v8p5857/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5857/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5857/r2.claim: The question in the verse is addressed in the afterlife to rebuke them.

JISHUMI:v8p5857/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5857/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5857/r3.claim: People have choice and action, shown by their being questioned and by the lifetime serving as evidence against them.

JISHUMI:v8p5857/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5857/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5857/r4.claim: The statement that wrongdoers have no helper means there is no intercession for major sinners.

SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r1.claim: ربنا is introduced by an implied speech verb, either specifying what they shout or as a circumstantial expression of their state.

SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r2.claim: يصطرخون is iftiʿāl from الصراخ, a loud cry, with ta changed to ṣād before ṭāʾ.

SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r3.claim: صالحا غير الذي كنا نعمل may both specify an omitted verbal noun or omitted object; alternatively صالحا modifies an omitted verbal noun and غير الذي is the object.

SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says adding غير الذي كنا نعمل heightens regret and admits their past wrongdoing; the apparent suggestion of further good deeds is resolved because they mistook their former conduct for good.

SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r5.claim: The Shaykh takes ما as a temporal verbal noun, meaning the duration in which one remembers.

SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r6.claim: The author rejects the temporal verbal-noun analysis because فيه refers back to ما, while only al-Akhfash and Ibn al-Sarraj allow a verbal-noun ما to be nominal.

SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r7.claim: ما is an indefinite noun qualified by a clause, meaning a lifetime or time in which a person remembers.

SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r8.speaker: الأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:35:37/r8.claim: Al-A'mash reads ما يذكر with assimilation, from اذكر; the Shaykh notes an unusual pronounced linking hamza in connected speech.

SAMIN-DURR:35:37#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:37#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:35:37#2/r1.claim: وجاءكم coordinates with أولم نعمركم, understood as قد عمرناكم, as in 26:18 and 94:1-2 where following clauses restate prior actions.

SAMIN-DURR:35:37#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:37#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:35:37#2/r2.claim: من نصير may be a subject governed by the preposition or a topic with the preceding prepositional phrase as predicate.

SAMIN-DURR:35:37#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:37#2/r3.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:35:37#2/r3.claim: A plural reading النذر is also transmitted.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r1.claim: Yaṣṭarikhūn means they cry out for help in Hell.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r2.claim: Their requested new deeds mean belief instead of unbelief and obedience instead of disobedience.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r3.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r3.claim: The span for reflection means reaching maturity, the first time of reflection.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومسروق
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r4.claim: One view sets the span at forty years.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r5.claim: A report attributed to Ali sets the span at sixty years.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r6.claim: Another view sets it at seventy, the last age for reflection before senility.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r7.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying God has excused a servant by extending life to sixty or seventy.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r9.speaker: الفراء والطبري
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r9.claim: The warner may be gray hair.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p476/r10.claim: Other interpretations of the warner are fever, deaths among relatives, or intellectual maturity.

MUJAHID:v2p532#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p532#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUJAHID:v2p532#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that on Resurrection Day people will be asked where those aged sixty are; sixty is the age mentioned in the verse about having enough life to remember.

MUJAHID:v2p532#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p532#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v2p532#2/r2.claim: A second report from Ibn Abbas says the verse refers to gray hair.

MUQATIL:35:37-39/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:35:37-39/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:35:37-39/r1.claim: The people of Hell cry for help, asking to return and do righteous deeds instead of associating partners with God.

MUQATIL:35:37-39/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:35:37-39/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:35:37-39/r2.claim: They are asked whether they had enough lifetime to take heed and whether Muhammad had warned them; they are told to taste punishment with no defender.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#2/r1.claim: Yaṣṭarikhūna is a form of ṣurākh, strenuous shouting, used for a loud, difficult cry for help; they ask to return and do differently.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#2/r2.claim: “Did We not give you time” may mean enough time for any receptive person to mend matters; rebuke is stronger for those given longer lives.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#2/r3.claim: The duration is variously said to be eighteen, forty, or sixty years.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#2/r4.claim: The warner may be the Messenger or the onset of gray hair; the construction coordinates it with the preceding question in sense.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p345#2/r5.claim: The sinners have no helper to assist them.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37/r8.claim: They cry for help in Hell with a loud voice; ṣarākh is a loud sound, ṣārik the one seeking help, and muṣrikh the helper.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37/r9.claim: A cited line uses the word ṣārikh for a frightened caller whose arrival is accompanied by the sound of hoofbeats; the poet is unnamed.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r1.claim: Their request is to leave Hell and return to worldly life.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r2.claim: He explains their promised righteous deed as saying There is no god but God.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r3.claim: Their request to do deeds other than before means replacing polytheism with faith, disobedience with obedience, and following the messengers' commands.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r4.claim: The question about giving them a period for reflection is the answer to their plea; an implied speaker introduces it.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r5.speaker: البخاري
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r5.claim: Bukhari titles a chapter that a person reaching sixty has received God's full excuse, citing this verse.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r6.claim: The Prophet says God has left a person's term long enough to reach sixty years; the report is transmitted through the chain Qurtubi supplies.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r7.speaker: الخطابي
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r7.claim: He explains aʿdhara ilayhi as granting the utmost excuse, illustrated by the saying that a warner has established his own excuse.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r8.speaker: الخطابي
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r8.claim: A person living to sixty has no remaining excuse: it is near death and an age for repentance, humility, anticipating death, and meeting God.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r9.speaker: علي وابن عباس وأبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r9.claim: They interpret the period in which a person can reflect as sixty years.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r10.claim: A sermon report says a divine caller addresses people over sixty with this verse and says warning has fully been delivered; no grading is stated.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r11.claim: A report cited from al-Tirmidhī al-Ḥakīm says that on Judgment Day people of sixty are called with this verse; no grading is given.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن البصري ومسروق
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#2/r12.claim: They identify forty years as the reflection period, a view Qurtubi calls sound because reason reaches its maturity at forty and later diminishes.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r1.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r1.claim: Mālik recalls learned people in his town pursuing worldly life, knowledge, and social contact until forty, then withdrawing to focus on the hereafter until death.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r2.claim: The Prophet says most of his community live between sixty and seventy, and few exceed that; no grading is stated.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r3.speaker: قراءة
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r3.claim: An alternate reading has the feminine plural warning word, wajāʾatkum al-nudhur.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r4.claim: The warning is interpreted as the Quran.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r5.speaker: زيد بن علي وابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r5.claim: They take the warning to mean the Messenger.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وسفيان ووكيع والحسين بن الفضل والفراء والطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r6.claim: They interpret the warning as gray hair.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r7.claim: Other interpretations identify the warning as fever, the deaths of relatives, or completed maturity; nadhīr also means warning.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r8.claim: Gray hair, fever, and relatives' deaths all warn of death; the Prophet calls fever death's forerunner, and al-Azharī explains it as death's messenger.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r9.claim: Gray hair warns that youth, associated with play and amusement, has passed; the cited poetry calls it a warning of death.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r10.claim: A line by an unnamed poet calls gray hair a warning of death; another speaker calls it a warning of one's lifetime.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r11.claim: The deaths of family, friends, and companions repeatedly warn the living of their own departure, as two cited poems express.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r12.claim: Mature reason discerns realities and moral distinctions, so the intelligent person works for the hereafter and seeks God's reward; this too is a warning.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#3/r13.claim: Muhammad was sent as both bearer of good news and warner, ending people's grounds for excuse, as two verses state.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#4/r1.claim: Taste means the punishment of Hell because they did not reflect or take heed.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:36-37#4/r2.claim: No helper for wrongdoers means no one can ward off God's punishment from them.

ZAJJAJ:v4p271/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p271/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p271/r2.claim: Their plea promises good deeds if released; God rebukes them for having had ample time to remember.

ZAJJAJ:v4p271/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p271/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p271/r3.claim: The time is interpreted as sixty years, sixty to seventy, seventeen years, or forty years.

ZAJJAJ:v4p271/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p271/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p271/r4.claim: The author says most interpretations take the warning messenger as the Prophet; others identify it with gray hair.

RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r1.claim: The cries do not reduce the punishment: their cries are sounds of the punished, and God does not ease it as an act of grace before they ask; they ask but receive no relief.

RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r2.claim: Their plea to be brought out shows their suffering is punishment, not correction: a pupil who admits wrongdoing would be released, while the punished person is not.

RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r3.claim: A captive may first hope for release without asking, then ask, and finally promise reform after a long stay when asking alone fails.

RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r4.claim: Those lost in this world remain lost in the next, as the verse says whoever is blind here will be blind in the afterlife.

RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r5.claim: They failed to recognize that return to worldly life is distant and impossible according to God's report.

RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r6.claim: Their vow to do good is unconditional and omits reliance on God, indicating self-reliance; God replies that sufficient time had been granted for reflection, faith, and action.

RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r7.claim: Their promise to do other than what they did exposes the corruption of their former deeds.

RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r8.claim: Believers acknowledge that God's grace, not their own knowledge or merit, gave them good; they need forgiveness more than further reward and ask God to act from grace, not strict justice.

RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r9.claim: God guides believers in the afterlife as He guided them in the world; their praise acknowledges their shortcoming and their reception of blessings beyond expectation.

RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r10.claim: The believers say they were settled in the lasting home by God's grace, admitting that their deeds are negligible beside His blessings; the disbelievers instead ask to return and work.

RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p26#3/r11.claim: The disbelievers' promise neglects God's majesty and avoids admitting that they cannot produce deeds proportionate to it; God had supplied both adequate lifespan and a messenger's guidance.

RAZI-FULL:v26p27/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p27/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p27/r1.claim: The stated obstacles to belief are either within the people, who failed to reflect on revelation, or in their guide, who failed to recite guidance to them.

RAZI-FULL:v26p27/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p27/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p27/r2.claim: “Taste” signals lasting punishment and is a command of humiliation; the wrongdoers have no helper when they need one because they placed words, deeds, and excuses wrongly.

RAZI-FULL:v26p27/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p27/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p27/r3.claim: One possible reading of “no helper” is that a wrongdoer is a person with compounded ignorance, mistaking falsehood for truth, and lacks beneficial knowledge in the afterlife.

RAZI-FULL:v26p27/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p27/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p27/r4.claim: Al-Razi's preferred broad sense is that no one can help them at all: God will not help, and there is no other helper; proof is called sultan because authority or power aids.

RAZI-FULL:v26p27/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p27/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p27/r5.claim: The singular “helper” here describes their actual presence in Hell after despairing of human allies and idols, leaving them to hope only for God; elsewhere the warning concerns worldly life or early gathering and expected idol-help.

STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r9.claim: The longest comparison of believers and disbelievers in verses 29–39 leads into a final contrast between God’s Power and idols, then the outcomes of disbelief.

STUDYQURAN:35:37/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:37/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:37/r1.claim: After witnessing the Resurrection and Judgment they denied and admitting sin, disbelievers seek reprieve and promise righteousness, as in their plea to be sent back.

STUDYQURAN:35:37/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:37/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:37/r2.claim: The warners sent to them and their lifetime to reflect were already a reprieve; repentance is not accepted once death confronts an evildoer or disbeliever.

STUDYQURAN:35:37/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:37/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:37/r3.claim: God rejects requests for return because even if sent back, wrongdoers would again do what they had been forbidden.

STUDYQURAN:35:37/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:37/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:37/r4.claim: Wrongdoers have no helpers because they turned away from God and the help He sent them during worldly life.

STUDYQURAN:35:37/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:37/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:37/r5.claim: This and related verses can be read as part of an extended discourse between God and Hell’s inhabitants.

TAB-FULL:v19p384/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p384/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p384/r2.claim: The damned cry out for God to take them from Hell so they can obey him instead of repeating their former disobedience.

TAB-FULL:v19p384/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p384/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p384/r3.claim: “Yaṣṭarikhūn” derives from the form iftiʿāl of “cry out”; its tāʾ changes to ṭāʾ because of the nearby articulation of ṣād and the resulting heaviness.

TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the life span that gives a person sufficient warning is forty years.

TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r2.speaker: مسروق
TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r2.claim: Masrūq advises anyone who reaches forty to be cautious toward God.

TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r3.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas identifies the life span as sixty years.

TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas also says sixty is the age at which God has given a person sufficient excuse.

TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r5.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says a caller will summon those who reached sixty, the age named in the verse.

TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r6.claim: The Prophet says God has removed a person's excuse by allowing him to reach sixty or seventy.

TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v19p384#2/r7.claim: The Prophet says that whoever is granted sixty years has been given sufficient time and warning by God.

TAB-FULL:v19p387/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p387/r1.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v19p387/r1.claim: ʿAlī identifies the life span that gives sufficient warning as sixty years.

TAB-FULL:v19p387/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p387/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p387/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers forty years because the report for sixty includes a transmitter requiring caution, and because understanding reaches maturity at forty while before and after it are diminished.

TAB-FULL:v19p387#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p387#2/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v19p387#2/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the warner as the Prophet and cites 53:56, “This is a warner from the former warners.”

TAB-FULL:v19p387#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p387#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p387#2/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes the warner to be gray hair.

TAB-FULL:v19p387#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p387#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p387#2/r3.claim: The rebuke addresses Quraysh: they had enough years for thoughtful people to reflect, repent, and heed God's messenger, who warned them of the punishment they now face.

TAB-FULL:v19p388/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p388/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p388/r1.claim: The condemned are told to taste Hell's punishment; no helper can rescue those who wronged themselves through disbelief from God's punishment.

TABATABAI:35:37-38/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:37-38/r1.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:35:37-38/r1.claim: Al-Majma explains iṣṭirākh as crying out and calling for help, derived from ṣarākh.

TABATABAI:35:37-38/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:37-38/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:37-38/r2.claim: The request to be brought out explains the cries; God's question about granting a life in which one could remember answers them, and the commands to taste punishment and the denial of any helper follow from that answer.

TABATABAI:35:37-38/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:37-38/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:37-38/r3.claim: The people of the Fire ask to return and do good unlike their former deeds, but are told that they had time and a warner, failed to believe, and have no rescuer from punishment.

TABATABAI:35:37/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:37/r3.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:35:37/r3.claim: A saying in Nahj al-Balagha sets the age by which God has given a person sufficient excuse at sixty years; al-Majma and al-Durr also transmit it from Ali.

TABATABAI:35:37/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:37/r4.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:35:37/r4.claim: A report says that on Judgment Day it will be asked where the sixty-year-olds are, identifying them as those given the life mentioned in the verse; other routes cite Sahl ibn Sa'd and Abu Hurayra.

TABATABAI:35:37/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:37/r5.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:35:37/r5.claim: Another reported interpretation makes the rebuke apply to someone who reached eighteen years; it is attributed to al-Baqir and transmitted in al-Faqih.

TABRISI:35:36-37/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:36-37/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:36-37/r2.claim: Some readers use singular bayyinah and others plural bayyināt: singular can mean the scripture or what the Prophet brought, while plural reflects each prophet’s proof or the scripture’s several kinds of evidence.

TABRISI:35:36-37/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:36-37/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:36-37/r3.claim: Iṣṭirākh is a cry for help, formed from iṣ-ṣurākh with tāʾ changed into ṭāʾ to match the emphatic ṣād while retaining a similar articulation point.

TABRISI:35:36-37/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:36-37/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:36-37/r4.claim: Maqt means hatred; maqtahu means he hated him, and the person hated is mamqūt or maqīt.

TABRISI:35:36-37/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:36-37/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:36-37/r6.claim: Their plea to return means they promise faith and obedience instead of disbelief and sin, but God rebukes them for having had enough time to reflect and learn.

TABRISI:35:36-37/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:36-37/r7.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
TABRISI:35:36-37/r7.claim: One report says the age that removes any excuse is sixty years; this is also one report from Ibn Abbas.

TABRISI:35:37-40/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:37-40/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:35:37-40/r1.claim: A prophetic report says that whoever is granted sixty years has received sufficient time and has no excuse.

TABRISI:35:37-40/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:37-40/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:35:37-40/r2.claim: Other views identify the adequate age as forty years, or as a rebuke specifically directed to an eighteen-year-old; the latter is reported from Wahb, Qatada, and al-Sadiq.

TABRISI:35:37-40/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:37-40/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:35:37-40/r3.claim: The warner is Muhammad, according to Ibn Zayd, al-Jubbāʾī, and others; alternatives identify him as the Quran, gray hair, deaths of relatives, or full maturity of reason.

TABRISI:35:37-40/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:37-40/r4.speaker: زيد بن علي
TABRISI:35:37-40/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Ali identifies the warner as the Quran; Ikrima and Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna identify it as gray hair and cite poetry to support that usage.

TABRISI:35:37-40/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:37-40/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:37-40/r5.claim: The condemned are told to taste their punishment and remorse, for no helper can repel it from wrongdoers.

THALABI:v8p114/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p114/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p114/r1.claim: يصطرخون means they call, seek help, and cry out; it is derived from صراخ, and both helper and supplicant may be called صارخ.

THALABI:v8p114/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p114/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p114/r2.claim: They ask to leave the Fire and do righteous deeds unlike their former deeds.

THALABI:v8p114/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p114/r3.speaker: قتادة والكلبي
THALABI:v8p114/r3.claim: They say the period of life in which a person could reflect was eighteen years.

THALABI:v8p114/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p114/r4.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v8p114/r4.claim: He says the period was forty years.

THALABI:v8p114/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p114/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v8p114/r5.claim: He says the period was sixty years.

THALABI:v8p114/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p114/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v8p114/r6.claim: The Prophet says a caller on Judgment Day will ask where the sixty-year-olds are, referring to the warning about being given time to remember.

THALABI:v8p114/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p114/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v8p114/r7.claim: The Prophet says God has removed the excuse of anyone whom He allows to live sixty years.

THALABI:v8p114/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p114/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v8p114/r8.claim: Reports from the Prophet put most of the community's lifespans and deaths between sixty and seventy, with few exceeding that range.

THALABI:v8p114/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p114/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p114/r9.claim: النذير means the messenger; Zayd ibn Ali instead says it means the Qur'an.

THALABI:v8p114/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p114/r10.speaker: عكرمة وسفيان بن عيينة ووكيع والحسين بن الفضل
THALABI:v8p114/r10.claim: They interpret the warning as gray hair, which signals approaching death.

THALABI:v8p114/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p114/r11.speaker: شاعر
THALABI:v8p114/r11.claim: An unnamed poet calls gray hair a warning of death and a signal to prepare with dignity.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p432/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p432/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p432/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says يصطرخون means they cry out for help.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p432/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p432/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p432/r2.claim: The word is an iftiʿāl form derived from صراخ, and the source cites the verbs اصطرخ and تصارخوا.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p432/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p432/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p432/r3.claim: Muqatil says their cry for help is the plea to be brought out so they can do righteous deeds.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p432/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p432/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p432/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the promised righteous deed as saying there is no god but God, and the prior deed as associating partners with Him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p432/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p432/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p432/r5.claim: In Ata's report Ibn Abbas says the period of life in which people may take heed is eighteen years; Qatada agrees.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p432/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p432/r6.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p432/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says the period is forty years, as does al-Kalbi, who specifies the servant's life after reaching forty.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r1.speaker: منصور عن هلال
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r1.claim: Mansur reports from Hilal that people of Medina used to devote themselves to worship when one of them reached forty.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Mujahid's transmission, interprets the age as sixty years.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r3.claim: The author prefers sixty, citing Abu Hurayra's report that the Prophet said a person reaching sixty has been given ample warning about his lifespan.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, Muqatil, and most exegetes identify the warning-bearer as the Prophet.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r5.speaker: عكرمة وسفيان بن عيينة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r5.claim: Ikrima and Sufyan ibn Uyayna instead identify the warning-bearer as gray hair.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r6.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r6.claim: Abu Ali says النذير is an active participle if it means Muhammad, but better treated as a verbal noun if it means gray hair.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r7.claim: The author prefers the Prophet interpretation because 33:45 and 48:8 describe Muhammad as a warner.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r8.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p433/r8.claim: Muqatil explains taste as taste the punishment, from which no protector can shield wrongdoers.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:34-37/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:34-37/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:34-37/r4.claim: They cry for help; the warned lifetime is one in which a person can take heed, identified here as sixty years.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:34-37/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:34-37/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:34-37/r5.claim: One interpretation identifies the warner as the Messenger.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:34-37/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:34-37/r6.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:34-37/r6.claim: Another interpretation identifies the warner as gray hair.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p793/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p793/r11.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p793/r11.claim: The people in Hell ask to be returned to worldly life so they can do righteous deeds.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p793/r12.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p793/r12.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p793/r12.claim: The ‘warner’ who came to them is the Prophet.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p793/r13.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p793/r13.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p793/r13.claim: Qatāda reports that the verse was revealed with a person aged eighteen in its purview.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p793/r14.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p793/r14.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p793/r14.claim: Qatāda says all speech attributed by God to the people of Hell occurs before the command in 23:108 that they be despised and not speak.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p794/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p794/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p794/r2.claim: The wrongdoers who have no helper are polytheists.

ELMALILI:35:32-37/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:32-37/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:32-37/r8.claim: Reported views on the lifetime sufficient for reflection range from sixty, forty-six, or forty years to puberty, twenty years, or any age from twenty to sixty; God knows its truth.

ELMALILI:35:32-37/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:32-37/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:32-37/r9.claim: The stated term applies to everyone who dies after puberty.

ELMALILI:35:32-37/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:32-37/r10.speaker: Peygamber
ELMALILI:35:32-37/r10.claim: A prophetic report gives sixty years as the maximum lifetime for reflection.

ELMALILI:35:32-37/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:32-37/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:32-37/r11.claim: After the stated lifetime, disbelief has no excuse.

ELMALILI:35:32-37/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:32-37/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:32-37/r12.claim: The warning that came refers to the subsidiary branches of religious rulings.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:36/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:36/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:36/r1.claim: Unbelievers who dismissed worldly warnings plead for another chance when faced with punishment, but their cries do no good; compare 23:107–108.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p306/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p306/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p306/r2.claim: Without faith and righteous deeds, wealth and children only increase a person's ruin.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p306/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p306/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p306/r3.claim: Worldly wealth and children are exposed to danger, and people cannot protect themselves from those risks.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p306/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p306/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p306/r4.claim: Ḍiʿf can mean equal in amount or many multiples without a fixed limit; the faithful receive manifold reward, not necessarily only double.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p306/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p306/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p306/r5.claim: The chambers promise enduring safety and reward, unlike worldly wealth and children exposed to danger; the faithful need not fear loss in the Hereafter.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p361/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p361/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p361/r2.claim: In Hell, the condemned plead for release so they can return to the world and act differently from before.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p361/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p361/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p361/r3.claim: God answers that they had enough life to heed the reminder and a warner came; they receive no further support and must taste their deserved punishment.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p361/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p361/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p361/r4.claim: Those given sufficient lifespan and a warner who conclusively communicates truth receive no concession; people who die before maturity are treated more leniently.
